modes.note: One DOM, two token sets; --bg/--ink/--line/--signal/--mute swap on the root and every colour property transitions 600ms.

heading.purpose: Section titles; balanced wrap, 44px below, no separate mobile size.

org.purpose: Employer names heading each work group.

skill-tier-1.purpose: Skills taking most working time (back-end, mobile).

skill-tier-3.purpose: Everything else; dot separators in mute.

subtitle.purpose: Role line, project summaries, contact note, experience roles.

small.purpose: Tags, nav, hints, definition labels, "Also" heading, footer. Sentence case.

annotation.purpose: Redlines, corner tags, chain nodes, HUD; backstage only.

extensions.elevation: Flat. No box-shadow anywhere; depth is the mode flip, hairlines, and the bar sharing the page ground with one bottom rule.

motion.name: load-chars

motion.name: toggle-chain-draw

motion.name: row-plus

motion.name: cable-scroll

narrative.overview:
The site is one page with two faces. The *front* is the surface a visitor reads: a huge condensed name, bone-white ground, navy ink, hairlines, and almost nothing else. The *backstage* is the same page inspected: the ground turns blueprint blue, amber redlines measure the hero, every project row and every skill rung grows a drawn chain of evidence beneath it, and a small panel lists the anime.js timelines actually running with live progress. Nothing is added in backstage that the front hides; it is the same content annotated. The switch that flips them is the single bold element, and the rest of the page stays disciplined so the mechanism reads as the message: *what the user sees, and what makes it work*.

Density is editorial: one column of long text, generous vertical rhythm, a wide right margin reserved for annotations. Hierarchy is carried by type size and the condensed width axis, never by colour, boxes or badges. Confirmed rejections: card grids, stat heroes, eyebrow labels, gradients, glass, skill bars or percentages, monospace as decoration in the front.
keyCharacteristics: Two token sets on one DOM, switched by `data-mode` on `<html>`; colours transition natively (600ms), anime.js animates only the knob, staggers and SVG draws.
Ledger rows grouped under employer names instead of cards; hairlines carry all structure.

One grotesque, two registers: the condensed axis (wdth 75, opsz 96/60) marks the top of every hierarchy (name, section headings, employer names, tier-1 skills); everything below it is the same face at normal width, opsz 30 or 17.
Mono appears only where it is content (annotations, chains, "under the hood").
One orchestrated load sequence, one scroll-linked line, motion otherwise only on action.

rules.name: The One Marker Rule
rules.body: The signal colour has three roles: the knob, the focus ring, and backstage annotation (redlines, tags, chain nodes, HUD). It never colours body text, headings or backgrounds. If it starts doing so, it stops being a marker.

rules.name: The Same Page Rule
rules.body: Backstage may recolour and annotate, but never rearranges, hides, or adds copy that the front does not carry (the only exception is "Under the hood", which is technical detail, not a claim).

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No label above a heading. Definition-list labels ("The problem", "What I did") sit inside expanded case studies only, where they structure a sequence. The skill group label sits beside its rung, not above it.

rules.name: The Mono Is Content Rule
rules.body: Azeret Mono never appears in front mode.

rules.name: The Size Is The Ranking Rule
rules.body: In the skills ladder, type size and weight are the only ranking device. No bars, percentages, badges or colour steps.

rules.name: The Flat Drawing Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If an element needs separation, it gets a hairline, not a shadow.

dos: Do keep every new element readable in front mode with motion off; backstage is additive.
Do reserve the signal colour for the knob, focus ring and annotations.
Do put technical detail in "Under the hood" (backstage) rather than inflating the front copy.
Do use hairlines (1px, `--line`) for all structure; never boxes with backgrounds.
Do use the condensed axis (wdth 75) only at the top of a hierarchy: name, section heading, employer, tier-1 skill. Rows, subtitles and body stay at normal width.
Do rank by type size alone; when something new needs a hierarchy, pick a tier that already exists.
donts: Don't add cards, shadows, gradients, glass, icon tiles, bars, percentages or badges.
Don't use the mono face in front mode, and don't use it at sizes above 13px anywhere.
Don't add per-section entrance animations; the page has one load sequence, one scroll-linked line, and one toggle timeline.
Don't introduce a third colour family; extend within bone/navy and blueprint/amber.
Don't persist the mode between visits; every visit starts on the front (the `#backstage` hash is the only way to open flipped).
